history.summary: IDENTITY UNVERIFIED — PLACEHOLDER. No shrine named 'Bajali Satra' was found in any consulted source: Wikipedia's List of Satras, the GLC College thesis 'Barpeta - Land of Sattras' (which tabulates ~40 Barpeta/Bajali satras), the NBU socio-religious study of Barpeta satras, travel sites, and a geocoder POI search all came up empty. The name appears to be a generic label for a satra in the Bajali region. Documented satras of that region that this row may intend include: Akaya Satra (attributed to Sankardev, c.1500 AD, listed as 'Barpeta (Bajali)'), Bhawanipur/Kaljhar Satra (founded by Gopaldev 'Bhavanipuria Ata', about 7 km from Pathsala), and Gobindapur Satra (founded by Bhagawandeva, 1548 AD, Bajali) — plus Bamakatha (1626), Saibari (1565), Bhaluki (1688) and Siddhapur (1588) satras. CSV town 'Barpeta' is imprecise: Bajali was carved out of Barpeta district (first declared January 2021, restored as a district in October 2023) with headquarters at Pathsala; town and district are corrected to Bajali. Coordinates are for the Bajali locality and are approximate. No reliable on-topic image was found after genuine searching, so media is intentionally empty. name: Bajali Satra
town_description: Bajali, headquartered at Pathsala, is a district of Lower Assam carved out of Barpeta — first declared in January 2021, re-merged in December 2022, and restored as a district in October 2023. A fertile rice-and-jute agricultural belt, it is dotted with historic Vaishnavite satras and known for Pathsala's educational institutions and performing-arts tradition.

travel.airport: Lokpriya Gopinath Bordoloi International Airport, Guwahati (approx. 110-120 km).
travel.railway: Pathsala station; Barpeta Road (Simlaguri) is the nearest major junction.
travel.road: On the NH 27 corridor; Pathsala, the district HQ, is the main town and transport hub of the area.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March (general for Lower Assam satras); Doul Utsav season (February-March) for festival culture.
